script: My parents saw my new cabin, but I didn't invite them—why?. I (f46) live about 1000 miles away from my family. My husband and I snagged a few acres of forest land a couple years ago, thinking about a cabin or a retirement pad. It's an hour from where my sister lives and a couple of hours from my parents, who are 75. I've only ever driven around it; never actually hiked it. When I was planning a solo trip this summer, I called Mom to hash out logistics. "I want to explore the property for a day," I said. "Anyone who wants to join is invited, but I don't want to feel rushed." I dropped the fact that Dad is a total impatient wreck. He'll play a game for five minutes, snap, and then everyone just quits. He's super generous, so we don't want to make him sad, but he still ruins things. Mom got the vibe. We arranged for Sis to pick me up, we'd stay a night at her place, hit the property an hour away, hike, chill in town, then drive a couple of hours to my parents' house for the rest of my visit. I was hyped—everything felt solid. Then Dad shows up, saying he wants to see the property too. Mom hadn't talked to him. I said, "That's fine, but I really need to keep it chill. No rush, no pissed vibes." He just replied, "We'll just not go then." The whole convo. We've been acting like he never even tried to join, but I know he's feeling left out. I don't want him sad, but I might not get back to this spot for two years, and it's not the first time he's ruined my plans. I just wanted to enjoy it, you know? So am I the jerk for not inviting my parents to explore my new property with me, a couple hours from their house? Update: People suggest driving separately. That works, but we've got to lay out that we're not leaving at the same time. They love packing whole days where everyone goes everywhere together. The idea of splitting into smaller groups is lost on them. It's exhausting.
